question: What Does the WordPress Site Health Tool Actually Check?
metaDescription: A built-in diagnostic covering PHP version, security, performance and debugging info — worth checking periodically, though not every flagged item is urgent.
shortAnswer: Site Health (under Tools → Site Health) is a built-in diagnostic screen checking a range of technical factors: PHP version currency, HTTPS status, whether scheduled tasks (WP-Cron) are running correctly, REST API availability, and various security and performance recommendations. It's a genuinely useful starting point for a health check, though not every item flagged there is equally urgent — some are best-practice suggestions rather than active problems.

bodyHtml:
What Site Health Actually Checks

The tool runs a series of automated checks covering server environment (PHP version, required extensions), security-relevant settings (HTTPS, file editing permissions), performance-related factors (whether recommended caching or object caching is detected), and whether background processes like scheduled tasks are functioning. Results are grouped into "Critical" issues and "Recommended improvements," giving a rough sense of priority.

How to Interpret the Results

  • Critical issues genuinely deserve prompt attention — these tend to represent real, functional problems (an outdated PHP version well past its own support window, for instance).
  • Recommended improvements are more of a mixed bag, ranging from genuinely valuable suggestions to items that may not apply meaningfully to every site's specific situation — use judgment rather than treating every recommendation as mandatory.
  • The Info tab (separate from the health check results) provides detailed environment information useful when seeking technical support, since it exports a comprehensive snapshot of the site's configuration.
  • This tool doesn't replace a full security scan or performance audit, since it checks a defined set of common factors rather than performing deep, site-specific analysis.

Using Site Health Effectively

  1. Check Site Health periodically, not just when something already seems wrong.
  2. Address Critical issues promptly.
  3. Evaluate Recommended items against the specific site's actual needs rather than treating every one as mandatory.
  4. Use the Info tab's export when seeking technical support, to provide detailed environment context quickly.

Need help addressing issues Site Health has flagged? See WordPress bug fix.
